title: Domain
description:
A logical grouping that cuts across the containment tree. Racks are physical; an InfiniBand fabric, an NVLink domain, a Slurm partition and a power zone are not, and none of them nest neatly inside a rack.

This is the entity each team scopes its own view with. The IB team cares about `ib_fabric` domains, the Ethernet team about `ethernet_fabric`, OVA about `compute` and `cooling`, and facilities about `power`. One domain entity with a class discriminator means a team can filter to its own concern without every team needing its own entity -- which is precisely the duplication the contract exists to stop.

name.description: Name as the owning team uses it. For an NVLink domain on a GB200 NVL72 this is typically the rack, because the domain and the rack are coextensive there.

parent_id.description: Enclosing domain, for the cases that genuinely nest: an IB subnet inside a fabric, a partition inside a cluster. Not a general-purpose hierarchy -- a domain whose parent is of an unrelated class is a modelling mistake.

member_resource_ids.description: Explicit membership. Present for domains whose membership is a decision rather than a consequence -- a Slurm partition, a tenant allocation. Omit it where membership follows from the topology, because a stored list that duplicates a derivable one will disagree with it.

scope.description: Free-text bound on the domain's extent: a site, a hall, a cluster name. Advisory.

owner.description: Team or person accountable for this domain. Named because 'who do I call about this fabric' is the first question of every escalation, and an inventory that cannot answer it sends people to Slack to guess.
